name: Eigenoid
one_line: Lets one team's AI agent find and consult the specialist agent of the team that owns an answer, through a registry where discovery grants no access and the owning team decides what is shared.

asked.by: Dinis, met at the summit; relayed by attendees.1.fringe@PrompTugal.dinis

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: 'When one team's AI agent needs an answer another team owns, it asks that team's agent'; people step in only for questions that need a human.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: One registry lists agents wherever they run (AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, on-premises), each with its owner, team, environment and status.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: Control: 'Finding an agent grants no access'; the owning team sets what is shared and what needs sign-off; every exchange is recorded.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: Eigenoid Connect is a hosted service with a public agent registry and token access; Eigenoid Enterprise is self-hosted, with an internal registry, access controls and compliance evidence reports for reviewers and auditors.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: Enterprise can record identity, authorization decisions, policy versions, delegation and human approvals.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: Its security page says: 'Connecting agents does not contain their runtimes'; the endpoints' tools, permissions and security remain part of the boundary.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: A governance readiness review: 45 minutes on one workflow where two agents share context, with a one-page gap report mapped to EU AI Act Articles 9, 12, 14, 15, 17, 19, 26 and 72. It says it does not certify compliance.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: It publishes the limits of its evidence (as of 6 September 2026): implementation findings, not an independent security audit; no external user has yet validated a substantive Connect task.

told: Dinis sees going to market together as partners, Eigenoid and RiskMandate.
domain_note: No domain was given. eigenoid.com (Eigenoid, Tallinn; agent-to-agent discovery and connection) is the only live match found; eigenoid.ai, .io, .co and others do not resolve. Not yet confirmed by the company.

help.label: Our hypothesis, not their claim. Built from public pages only; nothing of theirs was tested.
help.pitch: Eigenoid governs what passes between agents: who may ask, what the owning team shares, and a record of each exchange. Its own security page draws the line: 'Connecting agents does not contain their runtimes.' That line is where RiskMandate works: for each agent on either side, its written mandate, what its credentials and tools actually reach, and the gap. Together, the exchange and the endpoints are both evidenced.

mandate.text: Each specialist agent's listing says what it answers and what its team allows it to share: a mandate, written by the owning team.

reach.text: Agents run on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and on-premises with their own tools and permissions; the endpoints 'remain part of the boundary' (its words). What each one can reach is outside what the registry records.

gap.text: Between what an agent is allowed to share through Eigenoid and what its runtime could reach and send by other paths: unknown from public pages, and measurable per agent.

together.label: Our suggestions. Nothing here is agreed.

items.title: A joint offer: the exchange and the endpoints
items.text: Eigenoid records who asked, what was shared and under which policy; RiskMandate measures what each agent at either end can reach. One evidence pack for a reviewer. Our suggestion, from what Eigenoid publishes.

items.title: Their readiness review plus our measurement
items.text: Its 45-minute review of one two-agent workflow, with RiskMandate's mandate, reach and gap for the same two agents added to the gap report.

items.title: Field-log material
items.text: Its articles on coding agents and Article 72 sit beside our harness runs: a shared write-up of one workflow, run and measured.
